The example contradicts itself, because its own part (b) prints \(4.818 \times 10^{23}\), which is \(2 \times 2.4088 \times 10^{23}\) and not \(2 \times 2.4098 \times 10^{23}\ (= 4.8196 \times 10^{23})\). [Textbook misprint: TWO of the four options are incorrect statements as printed, so the question does not have a unique answer as it stands. Besides the keyed option, the book also prints "The centres of spheres in octahedral voids are at the apices of a regular tetrahedron" — an octahedral void is surrounded by SIX spheres whose centres lie at the apices of a regular OCTAHEDRON (§1.6.1), and "tetrahedron" there is a misprint for "octahedron". The keyed answer is the claim that N atoms give 2N octahedral voids, because that is the statement the chapter's own Remember box in §1.6.3 directly refutes ("number of tetrahedral voids is 2N and that of octahedral voids is N") and the one this question is set to test.]

[Textbook misprint: the question omits the density of the element, without which it cannot be solved — both formulas needed, \(\text{unit cells} = x/(\rho a^3)\) and \(\text{atoms} = xn/(\rho a^3)\), require \(\rho\), and the stem supplies only the edge length and the mass. The book's own printed answers \(1.16 \times 10^{24}\) and \(2.32 \times 10^{24}\) are reproduced exactly by \(\rho = 7.2\ \mathrm{g/cm^3}\): back-solving from the printed answer gives \(\rho = 200/(1.16 \times 10^{24} \times (2.88 \times 10^{-8})^3) = 7.22\ \mathrm{g/cm^3}\), and the implied molar mass \(200 \times N_A/(2.32 \times 10^{24}) = 51.9\ \mathrm{g/mol}\) is that of chromium, which is indeed bcc. The missing datum is therefore "the density of the element is \(7.2\ \mathrm{g/cm^3}\)", and it is restored in the solution below. The book's printed answers are correct once it is supplied.]
